title: Lambda cold starts and provisioned concurrency
hook: A cold start creates a new execution environment — initialization latency matters for interactive APIs; provisioned concurrency keeps environments warm.

blocks.text: Cold starts occur on first invoke or when Lambda scales concurrent executions beyond warm pool. Init includes runtime bootstrap and loading handler code. Provisioned concurrency pre-creates initialized environments. VPC-attached functions historically added ENI setup latency — improved with Hyperplane. Java and .NET typically longer init than Node.js and Python.

blocks.text: P99 latency SLAs fail if cold starts dominate traffic spikes. Provisioned concurrency has hourly cost even without traffic. Right-sizing package and avoiding unnecessary VPC attachment reduces init.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: cold = init + handler; measure InitDuration; provisioned concurrency for steady low-latency; shrink package and avoid VPC if possible.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Measure
items.body: CloudWatch InitDuration and duration P99 on new version.

items.title: Optimize package
items.body: Tree-shake deps, Lambda layers for shared libs, avoid fat bundles.

items.title: Avoid VPC if possible
items.body: Public Lambda for AWS API calls; VPC only for private RDS.

items.title: Provision concurrency
items.body: Set on alias for prod; balance cost vs latency SLA.

diagram.title: Cold vs warm invoke
diagram.source:
flowchart TB
  Req[Request] --> HasWarm{Warm env available?}
  HasWarm -->|yes| Handler[Handler only\nlow latency]
  HasWarm -->|no| Init[Init runtime + code\nInitDuration]

snippet.label: Put provisioned concurrency
snippet.explanation: Apply to published alias — not $LATEST. Bills hourly per PC unit.

snippet.label: Alias with provisioned concurrency
snippet.code:
ProdAlias:
  Type: AWS::Lambda::Alias
  Properties:
    FunctionName: !Ref ApiHandler
    FunctionVersion: !GetAtt ApiHandlerVersion.Version
    Name: prod
    ProvisionedConcurrencyConfig:
      ProvisionedConcurrentExecutions: 10
snippet.explanation: Blue/green: shift traffic between versions with weighted alias.

snippet.label: Publish version and alias
snippet.code:
aws lambda publish-version --function-name ApiHandler
aws lambda create-alias \
  --function-name ApiHandler \
  --name prod \
  --function-version 5
snippet.explanation: Provisioned concurrency requires published version or alias.

snippet.label: CloudWatch InitDuration query
snippet.code:
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics \
  --namespace AWS/Lambda \
  --metric-name InitDuration \
  --dimensions Name=FunctionName,Value=ApiHandler \
  --start-time 2026-09-14T00:00:00Z \
  --end-time 2026-09-14T23:59:59Z \
  --period 3600 \
  --statistics Average,Maximum
snippet.explanation: Correlate deploy times with init spikes.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Provisioned concurrency on $LATEST — not supported. Enabling VPC for S3 access only — adds init without benefit. Ignoring InitDuration blaming handler code alone.

blocks.text: Lambda SnapStart for Java and upcoming patterns reduce init. Graviton2 arm64 often faster/cheaper. How to prove it in production: X-Ray cold trace flag, InitDuration alarm on new deploys, load test after publish before full traffic shift.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Blaming all latency on handler without InitDuration gets rejected. Strong answer: measure init, PC on alias, package diet, VPC only when needed.

interviewTakeaways: Cold starts add InitDuration before handler runs.
Provisioned concurrency on published alias pre-warms environments.
Shrink deployment package and limit VPC to reduce init.
60s: InitDuration metric. PC on prod alias. Small package. VPC only for private resources. SnapStart for Java.
Follow-up: does PC scale automatically with traffic?
commonPitfalls: Strong answer: publish version, alias prod, PC on alias.
VPC for all functions including S3-only — unnecessary cold penalty.
Fat node_modules in deployment zip slowing init.

jsTsCorrelations.note: await import() heavy modules inside handler defers init cost on warm paths — trade first cold vs steady state.
Single tree-shaken dist/index.js reduces cold vs full node_modules — like webpack prod bundle for server.
